 Advertisement Trump administration drops appeal to overhaul Public Service Loan Forgiveness program
 The Trump administration has dropped its effort to overhaul the Public Service Loan Forgiveness program. Here's what that means for the millions who rely on the program.

 The Trump administration has dropped its effort to overhaul the Public Service Loan Forgiveness program. Here's what that means for the millions who rely on the program.
 Updated: 4:55 PM EDT Oct 22, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Amy Lu Washington Correspondent Jailyn Anderson WASHINGTON — The Trump administration dropped its appeal to overhaul the Public Service Loan Forgiveness program , leaving the program unchanged for now. 
 The decision comes as a surprising reversal for many borrowers who view the program as a financial lifeline. Currently, more than 2.5 million borrowers are enrolled in the PSLF program, with a total loan balance of over $228 billion, according to Student Loan Planner . 
 Advertisement Under PSLF, borrowers must work for government agencies, public schools, hospitals, or eligible nonprofits and make 10 years of payments on their student loans to qualify for debt cancellation. 
 Last fall, the Trump administration introduced a rule granting Education Secretary Linda McMahon the authority to remove employers from the program if their work was deemed to serve "a substantial illegal purpose." 
 Critics argued the vague phrasing was intended to target employers who supported undocumented immigrants or transgender youth. 
 A federal judge later ruled that the administration’s plan overstepped agency power and threatened free speech. 
 With the appeal now dropped, the PSLF program remains unchanged, allowing eligible borrowers to continue working toward debt forgiveness.
